summary: Stamford Raffles worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served in the East India Company (~1795–1824) and was Lieutenant-governor of British Bencoolen (1818). In 1825, he founded the Zoological Society of London, becoming its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Lycée Pothier and Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He held posts at the Collège de France, Bibliothèque du Roi/nationale, and INALCO.

Stanislav Grof studied at Charles University (~1951–1956). He held positions at Kosmonosy Psychiatric Hospital, the National Institute of Public Health, Johns Hopkins University, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He founded the University of Warsaw in 1922, where he served as professor, and was later a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe worked in the fields of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He held an academic post at Duke University, attested in 1995 and 2004.
Stanley Cecil Sutton worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and later at the India Office Records (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler studied Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme, he served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale University (~1974–2012).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and Harvard as Esther and Sidney Rabb Professor of Anthropology.

Stanley Lombardo, a scholar of linguistics and philosophy, studied at Loyola University New Orleans, Tulane University, and the University of Texas at Austin. He held a long-term academic appointment at the University of Kansas (~1976–2014).

Stanley Weinstein specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa, Tokyo, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Komazawa, SOAS University of London, and served as professor at Yale University beginning in 1968.

Stanley Wolpert specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning his B.A. at City College of New York and M.A. at the University of Pennsylvania, he taught at UCLA from 1959, serving as department chair in 1967.
Stefan Anacker worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970), where he studied under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. After completing his dissertation at the University of Washington (~2002–2009), he held research posts at the University of Munich, Bavarian Academy of Sciences, and Göttingen Academy of Sciences.

Stefan Larsson works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Stockholm University under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm. He held appointments at UC Berkeley and the University of Gävle (attested 2019).

Stefan Mario Maul specializes in history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Göttingen and Freie Universität Berlin, he taught at Freie Universität Berlin before becoming Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University (1995) and leading a research unit at Heidelberg Academy.

Stefania Travagnin works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen (~2013–2020) before moving to SOAS University of London in 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Ca' Foscari, Sichuan, and Leiden, he held posts at Soka University, Ca' Foscari, and served as Yehan Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Oxford (2012–2020).

Steffen Döll works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Munich and Kyoto University. After assisting at Munich (2008–2015), he was appointed Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch specialized in Indology and art history. Educated at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski, she held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, and the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993).

Sten Konow was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oslo and Halle under Sophus Bugge and Richard Pischel. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India and held professorships at the Universities of Oslo and Hamburg.
